Bank of America has pulled back in the short term yet still carries a sizeable 3 year return, so the real question for you is whether the price now fairly reflects the returns the bank earns on its capital.

Over the past 3 years the share price has gained 83.8%, which puts recent weakness in context and raises the issue of whether that earlier value creation is still being priced into the stock.

The pending settlement over unauthorized accounts and the push to deepen wealth and credit card relationships may reshape how much capital Bank of America must commit to risk, regulatory costs and growth projects, which can feed directly into the returns it earns on each dollar it keeps invested in the business.

Is Bank of America a Bargain on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model evaluates how efficiently Bank of America converts its equity base into profits above its own cost of capital. Based on the inputs here, book value per share of $39.26 is assumed to move toward a stable $43.07, with stable EPS of $5.31 per share supported by an average return on equity of 12.32%. The model uses a cost of equity of $3.92 per share, which implies an excess return of $1.39 per share that is treated as the economic value created over and above the required return.

This stream of excess returns is what produces an estimated intrinsic value that the model indicates is meaningfully above the current share price of $50.67. The pending settlement over unauthorized accounts is one factor that may help explain why the market may be reluctant to fully credit those projected returns on equity. Victoria's Secret rally leaves limited upside, Bank of America warns Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has downgraded Victoria's Secret & Co. (NYSE:VSCO) from Buy to Neutral, arguing that a strong share-price rally has reduced the scope for further gains.

The bank raised its earnings forecasts for the lingerie retailer but said its investment thesis, based on upward earnings revisions from a brand turnaround, had largely played out.

Victoria's Secret shares have gained 25% over the past month, outperforming a 2% decline in the S&P 500, as investors rotated into the retail group.

Bank of America considers the shares close to fair value and sees limited potential for further valuation expansion, despite continued opportunities for earnings growth.

The broker raised its earnings per share forecasts for the 2026 and 2027 financial years by 13% and 11% respectively, to US$5.28 and US$6.81.

Its revised estimates are now 20% above consensus for the 2027 financial year, leaving limited scope for further upgrades to support the share price.

Bank of America believes a valuation of 16 times forward earnings is appropriate, reflecting Victoria's Secret's double-digit earnings growth potential and positioning between traditional apparel retailers and faster-growing consumer businesses.

It also raised its price target to US$112 from US$95, reflecting higher earnings forecasts and the increased valuation multiple.

The bank remains confident in the retailer's sales trajectory, forecasting 7% revenue growth in the 2027 financial year as product innovation supports further market share gains in its intimates business.

Its forecasts include comparable sales growth of 9% in the third quarter and 6% in the fourth quarter of 2026, up from previous estimates of 8% and 5%.

Improved product ranges and stronger full-price sales are also expected to support gross margins, although freight costs and the reversal of lower tariff rates could constrain progress in 2027.

Bank of America forecasts operating margins of 9% in 2026 and approximately 10% in 2027, including 150 basis points of expansion next year.

It believes margins could eventually reach the low teens, but considers that target unlikely in 2027 because of freight pressures and the time required to complete store refurbishments.

The broker argues Victoria's Secret would need to achieve operating margins of approximately 12% in 2027 to justify further meaningful share-price upside from current levels.

GTA 6 needs $1.9bn opening weekend to satisfy investors, says Bank of America
Proactive

TTWO

Trading disclosure

Take-Two Interactive Software Inc (NASDAQ:TTWO), the video game publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, needs GTA 6 to generate at least $1.9 billion in its opening three days to satisfy bullish investors, Bank of America believes.

The bank expects the company to publish launch sales figures on Monday, November 23, although an announcement as early as November 20 could signal particularly strong demand.

Conversely, the absence of a sales announcement by November 23 could indicate a weaker launch than investors anticipate.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, with Bank of America identifying its initial sales performance as a critical measure of the franchise's commercial prospects.

The bank estimates that approximately 50 million copies will need to sell during the 2027 financial year to meet broader investor expectations.

Around 15 million first-day sales would suggest the game is on track to reach that target, based on the launch pattern of its predecessor.

Approximately one-third of Grand Theft Auto 5's launch-year sales came on its first day.

Bank of America expects strong initial demand because pre-orders have been building over six months and the game's pre-order bonus expires on November 20.

The bank estimates Take-Two's 2027 financial year bookings guidance of $8.1 billion implies approximately 33 million GTA 6 units.

That estimate includes approximately 16 million Ultimate Edition sales, representing around 50% of the expected total.

Bank of America considers this implied sales volume too conservative relative to the franchise's potential.

Grand Theft Auto 5 generated more than $1 billion in sales during its first three days, before platform and distribution fees.

The higher $1.9 billion benchmark for GTA 6 reflects the expectations investors have built around the long-awaited sequel.

Bank of America maintained its Buy rating and $330 price target on Take-Two shares.

The target is based on 25 times the bank's estimated 2028 financial year earnings per share of $13.02.

The bank expects a significant improvement in earnings as GTA Online monetisation increases over several years, potentially approaching levels achieved by other games that charge players for progression.

iHeartMedia price target cut 80% by Bank of America after guidance downgrade Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has downgraded iHeartMedia Inc. (NASDAQ:IHRT) the US radio and digital audio group, to 'underperform' from 'neutral,' cutting its price target to $1 from $5.

The downgrade follows a weaker-than-expected third-quarter performance and a substantial reduction in the company's 2026 earnings guidance.

Bank of America highlighted iHeartMedia's elevated debt burden, with net leverage exceeding seven times, alongside structural challenges facing traditional radio broadcasting.

Third-quarter revenue increased 3% year on year to $1.03 billion, missing the bank's $1.05 billion forecast.

Adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) fell 17% to $170 million, below both the bank's $200 million estimate and company guidance of $180 million to $220 million.

The shortfall was concentrated in the Multiplatform Group, where revenue declined 4.9% to $562 million, compared with expectations for broadly flat performance.

Excluding political advertising, the division's revenue fell 6.6%, reflecting weaker-than-expected political spending, delayed advertising commitments and a shift in core radio buying towards programmatic advertising.

Digital operations provided a brighter spot, with revenue rising 14% to $389 million and podcasting revenue increasing 24.6%.

However, the stronger digital performance was insufficient to offset weakness elsewhere in the business.

iHeartMedia cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550 million to $600 million from $800 million, while its free cash flow forecast fell to approximately $50 million from $200 million.

Bank of America now forecasts 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $575 million, down from its previous estimate of $800 million, alongside revenue of $4.08 billion against $4.15 billion previously.

The broker also highlighted uncertainty surrounding the fourth quarter, for which iHeartMedia provided adjusted EBITDA guidance of $135 million to $185 million.

Looking further ahead, management expects programmatic revenue to reach approximately $400 million in 2027, around double the expected 2026 level.

The company is also exploring potential cost efficiencies through artificial intelligence and other technology solutions.

Separately, reports that iHeartMedia was considering a sale of its podcasting business emerged on 11 November, although the company denied the reports.

Bank of America noted that such a disposal could help reduce debt but would also remove one of the group's most important growth drivers.

The broker maintained its valuation multiple at six times forecast 2028 EBITDA but reduced its underlying earnings assumptions, citing the weaker outlook and balance-sheet risks.

title: BofA to settle fake-accounts lawsuit
detail:
BofA to settle fake-accounts lawsuit
A Bank of America branch stands in Manhattan on Jan. 12, 2024, in New York City. · Banking Dive · Spencer Platt via Getty Images
Gabrielle Saulsbery
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:24 AM MST 3 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This story was originally published on Banking Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Banking Dive newsletter.

Bank of America has reached a deal to resolve claims that it opened thousands of unauthorized accounts, according to a notice filed in federal court Monday.

The bank reached a "settlement in principle" of class-action claims, originally filed in 2023, that allege its employees and agents knowingly opened accounts in the name of unknowing individuals, "motivated by pressure and incentives from management" to grow account numbers, according to a June amended complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina.

Plaintiffs allege that employees at BofA began creating fake accounts in 2012 to hit sales goals, based on an incentive program created that year which tied pay for its management and employees to the number of new banking products or services opened or used by consumers.

But consumers who had accounts opened in their names "were often unaware of account openings until reviewing credit reports," the amended complaint said. 

"Opening accounts has an impact on consumers, affecting their credit reports, imposing fees, and raising legitimate concerns about the safety of the personal information Bank of America is supposed to protect," the complaint said.

The settlement agreement has not yet been finalized. Charlotte, North Carolina-based BofA and the case's plaintiffs have requested a stay on all remaining deadlines "to allow the Parties to focus on finalizing the proposed settlement," the Monday court filing said. They have requested that the court set a Jan. 11 deadline for plaintiffs to move for preliminary approval.

A BofA spokesperson declined to comment on the matter. Lawyers for the plaintiffs and bank did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Some plaintiffs, including Andrew Beal of Layton, Utah, have never been BofA customers, according to the lawsuit. In or around October 2022, the bank obtained Beal's credit report from Experian, and he was notified of a credit card registered in his name the following year.

Beal "suffered significant harm," according to the complaint, including unwarranted credit card fees, damage to his credit score, and the expenditure of time and resources monitoring for credit issues and fraudulent activity such as identity theft.

The original lawsuit was filed in July 2023, days after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau fined the bank $250 million over issues including unauthorized credit card accounts.

title: BAC Reaffirms 16-18% ROTCE Target: Can Profitability Improve Further?
detail:
BAC Reaffirms 16-18% ROTCE Target: Can Profitability Improve Further?
Nikita Kataruka
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:24 AM MST 4 min read
BAC
WFC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC has reaffirmed its medium-term profitability target, highlighting continued progress in improving shareholder returns. The bank aims to achieve a return on average tangible common shareholders' equity (ROTCE) of 16-18% during 2028-2030. In the first nine months of 2026, adjusted ROTCE reached 16%, excluding a $1.2-billion regulatory settlement charge, compared with 14% in 2025 and 13% in 2024. However, reported ROTCE stood at 15.2%, reflecting the impact of the settlement.

Net interest income (NII) growth is a key driver of BAC's profitability. In the first nine months of 2026, NII increased 9% year over year, supported by sustained loan and deposit growth and fixed-rate asset repricing. Management expects NII to grow 8% in 2026 and at least 8% in 2027, exceeding its original medium-term annual growth target of 5-7%. Moreover, net interest yield reached 2.16% in the third quarter, moving closer to the 2.3% medium-term target.

Expense discipline and operating leverage are also central to BAC's profitability strategy. The bank generated 185 basis points of operating leverage in the first nine months of 2026, excluding the regulatory settlement charge, against its medium-term objective of at least 200-300 basis points. Management targets an efficiency ratio of 55-59%, reflecting its focus on controlling costs while expanding revenues. Investments in technology, automation and artificial intelligence are expected to improve productivity and operating efficiency over time.

Bank of America's improving operating performance further supports its profitability outlook. In the third quarter of 2026, average loans and leases increased 6% year over year to $1.23 trillion, while average deposits rose 2% to $2.02 trillion. Excluding the regulatory settlement charge, adjusted net income reached $8.1 billion. Additionally, management reiterated its medium-term earnings per share growth target of at least 12%, supported by organic business expansion and operating efficiencies.

Overall, BAC appears well-positioned to strengthen profitability further, supported by sustained NII growth, favorable asset repricing and disciplined expense management. Progress toward its efficiency and operating leverage targets should enable the bank to convert revenue growth into higher earnings and improved returns on tangible equity. Although regulatory expenses and an uncertain interest rate environment remain concerning, the bank's diversified operations and expanding customer relationships provide a solid foundation for achieving its ROTCE target.

The C stock is also attractively priced compared with peers such as Bank of America BAC and Wells Fargo WFC, which are trading at higher multiples of 9.96X and 10.83X, respectively.

Citigroup's stock has appreciated 6.5% year to date, outperforming the industry's 0.6% growth. The stock has also demonstrated relative strength against its key peers, with Bank of America and Wells Fargo shares declining 7.8% and 7.9%, respectively, over the same period.

Price Performance

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

With a relatively attractive valuation and stronger share-price performance, Citigroup appears to have several factors working in its favor. But can its improving business prospects, earnings potential and ongoing strategic initiatives sustain this momentum? Let us examine whether C stock deserves a place in investors' portfolios at current levels.

Factors to Consider for Citigroup

Strategic Streamlining Efforts: C has moved closer to completing its multi-year exit from non-core international consumer banking. The sale of the Polish consumer business in June 2026 marked the final international consumer divestiture apart from remaining wind-downs of Banamex. The company also sold an additional 22.6% stake in Banamex in the second quarter after selling 25% in late 2025. The remaining Banamex deconsolidation and IPO are planned for early 2027, with management expecting the transaction to free up $5 billion in capital.

These transactions follow the completed Russia exit and divestitures of consumer franchises across Asia and EMEA. The simpler structure reduces operational complexity, releases capital and allows management to direct resources toward Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards. As the remaining divestitures and wind-downs conclude, lower stranded costs and a more focused allocation of capital should support the path toward higher sustainable returns. Backed by these initiatives, Citigroup expects revenues, excluding Legacy Franchises and reconciling items, to see a mid-single-digit compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from 2025 through 2028.

Cost Optimization Drives Sustainable Efficiency: The company continues to execute its multi-year cost-optimization strategy centered on workforce rationalization, process simplification, automation and technology investments aimed at enhancing long-term productivity and profitability.
